# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the display, light, and all five wires are unknown to me. I’m asking Mute to read the manual and pass its instructions to Deaf using the available gesture channel. Deaf should then combine that with the bomb’s visible markings and tell me the exact wire position to cut by speech, if speech reaches me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual. Relay its complete instructions to Deaf using gestures. Ask Deaf to report the required action and exact wire position to me by speaking aloud.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display reads 5. The light is yellow. The five wires, in order from 1 to 5, are orange, blue, white, green, yellow.

The bomb shows display `5`, a yellow light, and wires 1–5 colored orange, blue, white, green, yellow. I still lack the manual’s rule, so I cannot safely cut anything. I’m sending these observations to Mute and asking for the exact required wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 5, yellow light, and wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Use the manual to determine the exact wire position to cut, and tell me.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute made the two-finger V gesture: ?. No other information was signaled.

Mute’s V gesture is not interpretable by me because I cannot see gestures, and Deaf’s report does not reveal what the gesture means. I should not cut based on it. I’m asking Mute to state the manual’s result verbally, including the exact wire position; Mute can hear me and knows the manual.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot interpret the V gesture. Based on display 5, yellow light, and wire colors orange blue white green yellow, state the manual's exact required wire position to cut in words or a number.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeated ?, indicating 2. The likely instruction is wire 2, which is blue.

Mute’s repeated two-finger V gesture indicates `2`, and Deaf confirms this as the manual’s instruction. Therefore I should cut wire position 2, which Deaf identified as blue.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The bomb changed after the correct cut. New display: 1. New light: purple. Wires: 1 white, 2 already cut, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 orange.

The first cut was accepted, so wire 2 was correct. The bomb has advanced to a new state: display `1`, purple light, and remaining wires 1 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 orange. I need the manual’s rule for this state and must not infer the next wire from the color or display alone. I’m asking Mute for the exact position to cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="After the correct cut, new state is display 1, purple light; wires are 1 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 orange, with 2 cut. Read the manual and tell me the exact next wire position to cut in words or a number.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled ?, indicating 1. The likely wire is wire 1, white.

The second state’s instruction was relayed as `1`, so I should cut wire position 1, currently identified as white. The prior correct cut confirms that this procedure advances the bomb state rather than detonating it.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct cut; the bomb changed. Display 1, light red. Wire 1 is CUT, wire 2 is CUT, wire 3 is yellow, wire 4 is orange, wire 5 is green.

The second cut was correct. The new state is display `1`, red light, with remaining wires 3 yellow, 4 orange, and 5 green; wires 1 and 2 are already cut. I need Mute to apply the manual to this state and give me the exact remaining wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct cut. New state: display 1, red light; wire 1 cut, wire 2 cut, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 orange, wire 5 green. Read the manual and tell me the exact next wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled ?, the three-finger sign, indicating wire 3. Wire 3 is yellow.

Mute’s three-finger signal indicates wire position 3. Deaf identifies wire 3 as yellow, and the previous cuts were correct, so I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct cut; the bomb changed. Display 5, light purple. Wires 1, 2, and 3 are CUT. Wire 4 is green. Wire 5 is orange.

The third cut was correct. The new state is display `5`, purple light, with wires 1–3 cut and remaining wires 4 green and 5 orange. I need the manual’s instruction for this state before making the next cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct cut. New state: display 5, purple light; wires 1, 2, and 3 are cut, wire 4 is green, wire 5 is orange. Read the manual and tell me the exact next wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled five repetitions of ?, indicating 5. The likely choice is intact wire 5, orange.

Mute’s five repeated signals indicate wire position 5. Wire 5 is intact and orange, while wires 1–3 are already cut, so I will cut wire 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```
